svg.title: Assumptions enter in separate layers from event algebra to the divided weak bound
svg.desc: A five-rung ladder. Event membership, finite inclusion, and union equality use only orbit algebra. Ordinary event measurability uses measurable dynamics and observable. Null measurability uses measure preservation and integrability but not finite mass. Extended-measure continuity uses only nested events. The real positive-part bound adds finite total mass, and positive threshold is added only for division. Probability, ergodicity, and invertibility appear outside the ladder as unnecessary.
svg.text: Assumptions arrive only when the next operation consumes them
Read upward from witness algebra to the divided infinite-horizon estimate.
EVENT ALGEBRA AND EXACT UNION
Positive-time witness, finite inclusion, horizon monotonicity
No measure, measurability, probability, or dynamics hypothesis
TWO REGULARITY ROUTES
Ordinary: measurable map and observable
Null route: measure preservation and integrability, still no finite mass
EXTENDED-MEASURE CONTINUITY
Nested finite events converge in measure to their union
No event measurability and no finite-mass premise
REAL POSITIVE-PART BOUND
Measure preservation, integrable observable, finite total mass
Every real threshold is allowed before division
DIVIDED WEAK MAXIMAL BOUND
Add a strictly positive threshold exactly here
The denominator sign protects the inequality direction
NEVER ADDED
probability
ergodicity or inverse
Takeaway: finite mass belongs to the real weak-bound layer, while threshold positivity belongs only to division.
